1. Rajaraja Narendra ruled from Rajamahendravaram.
2. Rajaraja Narendra himself began the Telugu Mahabharata translation.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
86.x: Rajaraja Narendra ruled from Rajamahendravaram; it was his court poet Nannaya who began the Telugu Mahabharata, with the king as patron.
n: Rajaraja Narendra was associated with Rajamahendravaram. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #145 · pp 254-255]
Nannaya began the translation of the Telugu Mahabharata, known as the Andhra Mahabharatam. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #145 · pp 254-255]
xa: Rajaraja Narendra was **connected** with the **Chola royal family** through **marriage**.
He was crowned on **16 August 1022** and married **Ammanga Devi**, daughter of Rajendra Chola.
Nannaya's titles: **Adikavi, Vagadheeshwara, Shabda Shasanudu**.
Rajaraja Narendra's titles: **Kavyageetha Priyudu, Rajarajanarayana**.

86.s:
Match List-I (Inscription) with List-II (Significance):
List-I | List-II
a. Kalamalla | i. First Madhyakkara verse
b. Addanki | ii. First mention of the Kakatiyas
c. Bezawada (Yuddhamalla II) | iii. First Telugu verse, in Taruvoja metre
d. Magallu | iv. Earliest Telugu inscription (pre-Nannaya)
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
86.x: Kalamalla (c. 575, Renati Choda Dhananjaya) – earliest Telugu inscription; Addanki (Pandaranga) – first Telugu verse in Taruvoja; Bezawada (Yuddhamalla II) – first Madhyakkara verse; Magallu (Danarnava) – first mention of the Kakatiyas (not the Gajapatis).

86.s:
Consider the following statements about Nannaya:
1. His Andhra Mahabharatamu covers the Adi and Sabha parvas and part of the Aranya parva.
2. The Andhra Mahabharatamu is written in the Dvipada style.
3. He wrote the grammar Andhra Shabda Chintamani and bore the titles Vagadheeshwara and Shabda Shasanudu.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
86.x: Only two (1 and 3) are correct. 2 is wrong: the Andhra Mahabharatamu, the earliest surviving Telugu literary work, is in the Champu style (verse + prose).

86.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Narayana Bhattu was sent to Vengi as the representative of the Kalyani Chalukya Someshvara I.
2. The Nandampudi grant was composed by its donee Narayana Bhattu himself.
3. The Korumelli plates of Rajaraja Narendra were written by the same scribe as the Nandampudi grant.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
86.x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: Narayana Bhattu was the donee of Nandampudi village, but Nannaya composed the grant.

86.s:
Match List-I (Person) with List-II (Work / title):
List-I | List-II
a. Pavuluri Mallana | i. Ashtabhasha Kavisekhara
b. Vemulavada Bhimakavi | ii. Pavuluri Ganitamu
c. Nannaya | iii. Andhra Shabda Chintamani
d. Narayana Bhattu | iv. Kavijanasrayam
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
86.x: Pavuluri Mallana – Pavuluri Ganitamu (Telugu verse of Mahaviracharya's Ganitasarasangraham, first scientific text in Telugu); Vemulavada Bhimakavi – Kavijanasrayam; Nannaya – the grammar Andhra Shabda Chintamani; Narayana Bhattu – title Ashtabhasha Kavisekhara.

86.s: Which of the following cities was founded by the Eastern Chalukyas?
86.x: Rajamahendravaram (Rajahmundry) was built under the Eastern Chalukyas by Ammaraja I (Rajamahendra); Warangal is Kakatiya and Amaravati/Dhanyakataka Satavahana.

86.s: During whose times was Rajamahendri i.e. the present town of Rajahmundry built?
86.x: Rajamahendravaram (Rajahmundry) was built under the Eastern Chalukyas by Ammaraja I (Rajamahendra); Warangal is Kakatiya and Amaravati/Dhanyakataka Satavahana.

86.s: Which Chalukya king got the title 'Rajamahendra'?
86.x: Ammaraja I (Vishnuvardhana VI) bore the title Rajamahendra, after which Rajamahendravaram is named.

86.s: Who among the following kings built Rajahmundry?
86.x: Rajahmundry (Rajamahendravaram) was built by Ammaraja I (Rajamahendra), who shifted the capital there from Vengi; Rajaraja Narendra only ruled from it and made it famous.

86.s: Which Eastern Chalukya ruler built a temple to Kartikeya Swamy at Bezawada?
86.x: Yuddhamalla built the Kartikeya (Kumaraswamy) temple at Bezawada, recorded in his Bezawada inscription.

86.s: Who among the following kings built Rajahmundry?
86.x: Rajahmundry (Rajamahendravaram) was built by Ammaraja I (Rajamahendra), who shifted the capital there from Vengi; Rajaraja Narendra only ruled from it and made it famous (official G2 2008 key: Rajaraja Narendra).

86.s: Who of the following rulers built Rajahmundry?
86.x: Rajahmundry (Rajamahendravaram) was built by Ammaraja I (Rajamahendra), who shifted the capital there from Vengi; Rajaraja Narendra only ruled from it and made it famous.

86.s: Which Eastern Chalukya king built a new city called Rajamahendravaram?
86.src: APPSC Junior Assistants in Labs / Panchayat Raj 2012
86.x: Ammaraja I built the new city of Rajamahendravaram and shifted the capital there; Ammaraja II issued Jain grants.

86.s:
Consider the following statements: A. The City of Rajamahendravaram was constructed by Ammaraja Vishnuvardhana-I. B. In the Madras Presidency, the district of Rajamahendravaram was created in 1823.
Of the above, the correct statements are
86.src: Grama Ward Sachivalayam Category-II(B) VRO/Village Surveyor
86.x: Both are correct: Ammaraja I (Vishnuvardhana VI) built Rajamahendravaram, and the Rajahmundry district of the Madras Presidency was created in 1823 (split into Godavari and Krishna districts in 1859).

86.s: What was the name of the new city built by Ammaraja I (921-927), believed to be the cultural capital of the Andhras?
86.x: Ammaraja I (921-927) built Rajamahendravaram (Rajahmundry), later the cultural capital of the Andhras.

86.s: Rajamahendri (present-day Rajahmundry) was developed under which dynasty?
86.x: Rajamahendravaram (Rajahmundry) was built under the Eastern Chalukyas by Ammaraja I (Rajamahendra); Warangal is Kakatiya and Amaravati/Dhanyakataka Satavahana.

86.s: Rajamahendri (present-day Rajahmundry) was built during whose reign?
86.x: Rajamahendravaram (Rajahmundry) was built under the Eastern Chalukyas by Ammaraja I (Rajamahendra); Warangal is Kakatiya and Amaravati/Dhanyakataka Satavahana.

86.s: After whom did Bezawada take the name Vijayawada?
86.x: Bezawada came to be called Vijayawada after Vijayaditya.

86.s:
Consider the following statements about the capitals of the Eastern Chalukyas:
1. Pithapuram (Pishtapura) was the first capital, under Kubja Vishnuvardhana.
2. The capital was shifted to Vengi (Pedavegi, near Eluru) by Gunaga Vijayaditya III.
3. Ammaraja I made Rajamahendravaram the capital, and Rajaraja Narendra ruled from it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
86.x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: Jayasimha Vallabha I shifted the capital to Vengi; the order is Pithapuram – Vengi – Rajamahendravaram.

86.s:
Match List-I (Old name) with List-II (Place / region):
List-I | List-II
a. Andhra Nagaram | i. Pithapuram
b. Mangalapura | ii. Vengi
c. Venginadu | iii. Mangalagiri
d. Pishtapura | iv. Krishna-Godavari doab
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
86.x: Andhra Nagaram – Vengi (Dandin's Dashakumaracharita); Mangalapura – Mangalagiri (Kopparam / Marturu records); Venginadu – the Krishna-Godavari doab, the core territory; Pishtapura – Pithapuram, the first capital.

86.s: Kokkili belongs to which dynasty?
86.src: APPSC Assistant Social Welfare, Assistant BC Welfare & Assis
86.x: Kokkili Vikramaditya was an Eastern Chalukya prince (son of Mangi Yuvaraja, brother of Jayasimha II) who set up a kingdom at Yalamanchili after being ousted by Vishnuvardhana III.

86.s: Which of the following Eastern Chalukya kings got the title 'Vishama Siddhi' (Conqueror of the Forest)?
86.x: Kubja Vishnuvardhana I, founder of the Eastern Chalukyas, bore the title Vishamasiddhi (also Makaradhwaja).

86.s: Who bore the title "Kollabhiganda"?
86.x: Kollabhiganda was the title of Vijayaditya IV, son of Chalukya Bhima I, who ruled six months and died near Virajapuri fighting Kalinga.

86.s: Who bears the title "Kollabhiganda"?
86.x: Kollabhiganda was the title of Vijayaditya IV, son of Chalukya Bhima I, who ruled six months and died near Virajapuri fighting Kalinga.

86.s: Which of the following statements is NOT true about the Chalukyas of Vengi?
o: They initially ruled as subordinates to the Badami Chalukyas.
They were defeated and annexed by the Rashtrakutas.
Their dynasty lasted for over four centuries.
86.src: APPSC Assistant Tribal Welfare Officer in A.P. Tribal Welfar
86.x: The Vengi Chalukyas began as subordinates of Badami, promoted early Telugu literature and lasted 624-1075; they fought the Rashtrakutas for two centuries but were never annexed - they merged into the Chola line.

86.s: Which one of the following were the contemporaries to the Eastern Chalukyas in the south?
86.src: Social and Cultural History of AP and Welfare Programmes 201
86.x: The Pallavas of Kanchi were the southern contemporaries of the early Eastern Chalukyas (Jayasimha I clashed with them); the Ikshvakus were earlier, the Mughals later and the Palas in Bengal.

86.s: In which year did Eastern Chalukya rule begin?
86.x: Kubja Vishnuvardhana declared independence in 624 CE, beginning Eastern Chalukya rule.

86.s: Terms like 'kharidika', 'kharis' and 'nivartanas' were often used in the recorded literature during the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi. They were used to measure ____.
86.src: APPSC Junior Assistant in Dr. NTR University of Health Scien
86.x: Nivartana, kharidika and khari were Eastern Chalukya units of land area, based on the seed sown.

86.s: Kokili belongs to which dynasty?
86.src: APPSC Asst. BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Mains Paper-II 2017
86.x: Kokkili (Kokkili Vikramaditya, 8th c.) was an Eastern Chalukya king of Vengi who briefly succeeded Vishnuvardhana III and was overthrown. He was not a Pallava, Ganga or Chola ruler.

86.s:
Consider the following statements about the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi:
1. Sanskrit was their official language.
2. Most of their about 100 donation inscriptions are in Sanskrit.
3. Kannada was their official language.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
86.x: Sanskrit was the official language and most of the about 100 donation inscriptions are in Sanskrit. Kannada was not their official language, so 3 is wrong.

86.s: After 973 CE, who was the principal rival of the Eastern Chalukyas?
86.x: After 973 CE, the Kalyani Chalukyas emerged as the principal rival of the Eastern Chalukyas. Satyasraya and Someshvara I are associated with this later phase.
86.tq: Identify the change in the rival dynasty by using the chronological marker.
xs: After **973 CE** the main rival was the **Kalyani Chalukyas** — option **(4)**.
Kalyani kings involved: **Satyasraya** (**1006**) and **Someshvara I**.
xa: **Saktivarma I** beat Satyasraya's general **Bayyalanambi** with Chola help.
In the succession war **Kalyani Jayasimha II** backed **Vijayaditya VII**.
After **Koppam (1053)** Rajaraja Narendra had to accept **Kalyani suzerainty**.

86.s:
Assertion (A): The Eastern Chalukyas originated as a branch of the Badami Chalukyas.
Reason (R): Kubja Vishnuvardhana, the first Eastern Chalukya ruler of Vengi, was the brother of Pulakeshin II.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
86.x: Both are true: the Eastern Chalukyas branched from the Badami line because Kubja Vishnuvardhana, Pulakeshin II's brother, founded their rule in Vengi.
n: The Eastern Chalukyas originated as a branch of the Badami Chalukyas. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #145 · pp 254-255]
Kubja Vishnuvardhana was the brother of Pulakeshin II. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #145 · pp 254-255]
The core region of the Eastern Chalukyas was Vengi in present-day Andhra Pradesh. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #145 · pp 254-255]
Rajamahendravaram, also known as Rajahmundry, later became an important centre. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #145 · pp 254-255]
Rajaraja Narendra was associated with Rajamahendravaram. [Indian History · ROCKET SHEET #145 · pp 254-255]
xa: First capital: **Pithapuram**; **Jayasimha I** moved it to **Vengi**.
Emblem: **Boar (Varaha)**; official language **Sanskrit**.
Greatest ruler: **Gunaga Vijayaditya III** (APHQ 2011).
Inscriptions use the matronymic **"Hariti Putra"**.

86.s: Who was the last king of the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi?
86.x: Vijayaditya VII (1070-1075) was the last king; his death in 1075 ended the Vengi line.

86.s: Which of the following was a title of Kubja Vishnuvardhana?
86.x: Besides Vishamasiddhi, Kubja Vishnuvardhana had the titles Sarvasiddhi and Makaradhwaja.

86.s: Which of the following title–ruler pairs is NOT correctly matched?
86.x: Chalukya Chandra was the title of Saktivarma I, not Vimaladitya. Vimaladitya bore the titles Rajamartanda and Mummadi Bhima.
86.tq: Find the swapped ruler in a title table, especially where two rulers belong to the same dynastic phase.
xs: **Chalukya Chandra — Vimaladitya** is wrong — option **(1)**: Chalukya Chandra was **Saktivarman I**.
Vimaladitya's titles were **Rajamartanda** and **Mummadi Bhima**.
The others are right: **Narendramrigaraja** — Vijayaditya II; **Rajamahendra** — Ammaraja I; **Vishamasiddhi** — Kubja Vishnuvardhana.
xa: **Kollabhiganda** — **Chalukya Bhima I** (G2 2012 key).
**Tripura Martya Maheshwara** — **Gunaga Vijayaditya III**.
**Rajaraja Narendra**: Kavyageetha Priyudu, Rajarajanarayana, Baraganda Bhairava.

86.s: In 1006 CE, Satyasraya sent Bayyalanambi against Vengi. Who defeated Bayyalanambi?
o: Vijayaditya VII with Rajendra Chola's assistance
86.x: Saktivarma I defeated Bayyalanambi with Chola help in 1006 CE. Satyasraya of the Kalyani Chalukyas had sent Bayyalanambi against Vengi.
86.tq: Track the combatant, the opposing commander and the external support separately.
xs: **Saktivarma I** beat **Bayyalanambi** with **Chola** help in **1006** — option **(4)**.
Bayyalanambi was sent by **Satyasraya** of Kalyani.
xa: Saktivarma's coins are found in **Arakan (Burma)**.
He and **Vimaladitya** had recovered Vengi from **Jatachoda Bhima** with Chola help.
Title: **Chalukya Chandra**.

86.s:
Match the following:
List-I (Title)
A. Samasta Bhuvanashraya
B. Rajamartanda
C. Chalukya Chandra
D. Kollabhiganda
List-II (Ruler)
1. Saktivarma I
2. Vijayaditya IV
3. Jayasimha I
4. Vimaladitya
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
86.x: Samasta Bhuvanashraya - Jayasimha I; Rajamartanda - Vimaladitya; Chalukya Chandra - Saktivarma I; Kollabhiganda - Vijayaditya IV.

86.s: Kokkili, from whom Vishnuvardhana III took back the throne, set up which kingdom?
86.x: Kokkili set up the Yalamanchili kingdom; Vishnuvardhana III took the throne back from him.

86.s: Which Eastern Chalukya ruler issued the Chekurru copper plate?
86.x: The Chekurru copper plate belongs to Ammaraja I, who made Rajamahendravaram the capital.

86.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
86.x: The Eastern Chalukyas called themselves Haritiputras and their mother goddess was Hariti (APPSC G2 2019); Kushmandini is a Jain yakshi. Kalyanakaraka is Ugradityacharya's medical work, not a Shaiva school.
86.tq: Separate a deity name from a dynastic title, text and place name.

86.s:
Arrange the following Andhra dynasties in chronological order:
1. Kakatiyas
2. Eastern Chalukyas
3. Vijayanagara
4. Reddis
86.x: Eastern Chalukyas (624–1075) came first, then the Kakatiyas (1163–1323), the Reddis and Vijayanagara.

86.s: By what name is the Chalukya-Chola era in Andhra (1076–c.1210), the age of the Velanati Chodas, also known?
86.x: The Chalukya-Chola phase of 1076–c.1210 is known as the Mandalika Yugam, before the Kakatiyas (1163–1323) rose.

86.s: Who built the Kesari Samudra lake (Kesamudram)?
86.x: The Kesari Samudra lake was built by the Kakatiya Prola I, not Rudradeva.

86.s:
Consider the following statements about the beginnings of the Eastern Chalukyas:
1. Pulakeshin II took Vengi c. 616 after defeating the Vishnukundins.
2. Kubja Vishnuvardhana was made viceroy of Vengi in 617.
3. The Kopparam plates (631) of Pulakeshin II call Kubja Vishnuvardhana 'Maharaja'.
4. The Chipurupalli plates of Kubja Vishnuvardhana, found in Vizianagaram district, are of his 18th regnal year.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
86.x: Only three (1, 2 and 4) are correct. 3 is wrong: the Kopparam plates of 631 call Kubja Vishnuvardhana 'Yuvaraja'.

86.s:
Consider the following statements about the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi:
1. Their royal emblem was the boar (Varaha).
2. They ruled from 624 to 973 and ended with the rise of the Kalyani Chalukyas.
3. Like the Satavahanas, Ikshvakus and Kadambas, they used the matronymic Hariti-putra.
4. Tribhuvanankusa was the seal sign manual on their copper plates.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
86.x: 1, 3 and 4 are correct. 2 is wrong: they ruled 624–1075 (over four centuries); after 973 the Kalyani Chalukyas were only their main rivals.

86.s:
Match List-I (Eastern Chalukya ruler) with List-II (Event):
List-I | List-II
a. Vijayaditya I | i. Died at Virajapuri fighting Kalinga
b. Vishnuvardhana IV | ii. Defeated by Dhruva, who married his daughter Sheela Mahadevi
c. Danarnava | iii. Conflict with the Rashtrakuta Dantidurga begins
d. Vijayaditya IV | iv. Killed by Jatachoda Bhima
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
86.x: Vijayaditya I – conflict with Dantidurga begins; Vishnuvardhana IV – defeated by Dhruva, who married Sheela Mahadevi; Danarnava – killed by Jatachoda Bhima; Vijayaditya IV (Kollabhiganda) – ruled six months and died at Virajapuri.

86.s:
Consider the following statements about Chalukya Bhima I:
1. The Pithapuram inscription of Mallappadeva credits him with 360 battles.
2. He repelled the Rashtrakuta Krishna II at Koppam and Dharanikota.
3. His court singer and dancer Chellavva bore the title Gandharva-Vidya-Visarada.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
86.x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: Bhima I repelled Krishna II at Niravadyapura and Peruvanguru; Dharanikota and Koppam belong to the 11th-century Chola–Kalyani wars.

86.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. After the battle of Koppam (1053), Rajaraja Narendra had to accept the suzerainty of the Rashtrakutas.
2. Vimaladitya, who married Kundavai, was crowned in 1011.
3. Rajaraja Narendra, crowned in 1022, married Ammanga Devi, daughter of Rajendra Chola.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
86.x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: after Koppam (1053) Rajaraja Narendra accepted Kalyani Chalukya suzerainty; the Rashtrakutas had fallen by 973.

86.s:
Consider the following statements about the Vengi succession war of the 11th century:
1. Rajaraja Narendra, son of Kundavai, was backed by Rajendra I.
2. The Chola Rajadhiraja I was killed at Dharanikota by Ahavamalla Someshwara.
3. Vijayaditya VII, son of Melama, was backed by the Kalyani ruler Jayasimha II.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
86.x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: Rajadhiraja I won at Dharanikota and burnt Kollipaka, but was killed at Koppam by Ahavamalla Someshwara.

86.s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Rajendra Chalukya (Kulottunga I) united the Eastern Chalukya and Chola lines.
Reason (R): Kulottunga I married Kundavai, daughter of Rajaraja Chola I.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
86.x: A is true: Rajendra Chalukya = Kulottunga I, the first Chalukya-Chola king. R is false: he married Madhurantaki, daughter of Rajendra II; Kundavai married Vimaladitya.

86.s: Which dynasty gave prominence to Jain religion and worked for its propagation in Telugu land?
86.src: APPSC Asst. BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Mains Paper-II 2017
86.x: The Vemulawada Chalukyas (Karimnagar), patrons of Pampa and Somadeva Suri, did most to propagate Jainism in Telugu land; Baddega built the Subhadhama Jinalaya. The Eastern Chalukyas only patronised Jainism alongside Shaivism.

86.s: The great Vishnu temple of Kunti Madhava at Pithapuram was constructed by
86.src: APPSC Asst. BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Mains Paper-II 2017
86.x: The first Eastern Chalukya king, Kubja Vishnuvardhana, a Vaishnava, built the Kunti Madhava temple at Pithapuram.

86.s: Who built the 'Nedumbasadi' for the Jains?
86.x: Ayyana Mahadevi, Jain queen of Kubja Vishnuvardhana, built the Nedumbasadi at Bezawada for the Kavaruragana Jains (Musinikonda inscription).

86.s: Ayyana Mahadevi built the Jain temple ' Nedumba Vasati ' near Vijayawada. She was the queen of
86.x: Ayyana Mahadevi, who built the Nedumba Vasati at Vijayawada, was the queen of Kubja Vishnuvardhana.

86.s: Which Eastern Chalukya ruler promoted Jainism?
86.src: APPSC Junior Assistants in Labs / Panchayat Raj 2012
86.x: Vimaladitya was the only Eastern Chalukya king who converted to Jainism (guru Trikalayogi Siddhanti; Ramatirtha cave).

86.s: Who built the great Vishnu temple called Kunti Madhava Temple in Pithapuram?
86.src: APPSC Assistant Social Welfare, Assistant BC Welfare & Assis
86.x: The first Eastern Chalukya king, Kubja Vishnuvardhana, a Vaishnava, built the Kunti Madhava temple at Pithapuram.

86.s: Which of the following ruling dynasties gave great importance to Jainism and worked tirelessly to spread that religion in andhra desa?
86.src: APPSC Assistant Social Welfare, Assistant BC Welfare & Assis
86.x: The Vemulawada Chalukyas (Karimnagar), patrons of Pampa and Somadeva Suri, did most to propagate Jainism in Telugu land; Baddega built the Subhadhama Jinalaya. The Eastern Chalukyas only patronised Jainism alongside Shaivism.

86.src: APPSC Junior Assistant in Dr. NTR University of Health Scien
86.x: Bhima – Draksharama (3); Eastern Chalukyas – Pancharama kshetras (4); Rajaraja Narendra – Chalukya-Chola architecture (2); Kakatiyas – Shaivism almost destroyed Jainism (1).

86.s: Which grant records Queen Ayyana Mahadevi's Nedumba Vasati?
86.x: The Musinikonda grant of Vishnuvardhana III records Ayyana Mahadevi's Nedumba Vasati.

86.s: Which of the following is included among the Pancharamas associated with the Eastern Chalukya temple tradition?
86.x: Bhimarama and Draksharama are included among the key Pancharama temples mentioned in the Eastern Chalukya tradition.
86.tq: Recognise a Pancharama name rather than a nearby Bikkavolu or Pithapuram temple.
xs: **Bhimarama** is one of the **Pancharamas** — option **(4)**; **Draksharama** is another.
**Vijayeshwara** and **Chandrashekhara** are Bikkavolu temples; **Kunti Madhava** is at Pithapuram.
xa: The Pancharamas were built by **Chalukya Bhima I**.
**Bhimeswara** temples: **Draksharama** and **Samalkot**.
Dominant faith: **Shaivism**.

86.s: Which faith was dominant under the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi?
86.x: Shaivism was dominant; the dynasty was tolerant and also patronised Jainism and Buddhism.

88.s: The ____ dynasty ruled over Andhra country from 12th to 13th centuries.
88.src: Social and Cultural History of A.P and Welfare Programmes 20
88.x: The Kakatiyas ruled the Andhra country in the 12th-13th centuries (independent from 1163 to 1323) from Hanumakonda and Orugallu. The Western Chalukyas and Cholas were earlier, the Yadavas ruled Maharashtra.

88.s: One of the major dynasties that ruled over Andhra
88.x: All four ruled parts of Andhra, so the question is loose; the intended answer is the Satavahanas, the first and greatest major dynasty of Andhra (the Kakatiyas were the second to unite all Telugu lands). Keyed as printed.

88.s: The Dynasty which had given ultimate design to Andhra culture and civilisation was
88.x: The Kakatiyas united the whole Andhra region and 'gave a comprehensive form to Andhraism' - Telugu identity, Orugallu as Andhranagari - so they gave Andhra culture its final shape. The Satavahanas, Pallavas and Chalukyas came earlier.

88.s: Which of the following clans the first rulers of Jains are believed?
88.x: The Kakatiyas were initially Jains and later embraced Shaivism, so they are the clan whose first rulers were Jains. The Satavahanas were Brahmanical, the Guptas Vaishnava, the Reddis Shaiva.

88.s: Bayyaram inscription tells about whose history?
88.x: The Bayyaram tank inscription of Mailamba (Ganapatideva's sister) gives the genealogy of the early Kakatiyas from Venna Bhupati. It has nothing to do with the Reddis, Badami Chalukyas or Satavahanas.

88.s: Who was the Raja Guru of Ganapatideva?
88.x: Visvesvara Sivacharya (Visvesvara Siva), head of the Golaki Matha, was Ganapatideva's raja guru. Vidyanatha was Prataparudra's court poet; Mallikarjuna Pandita and Sripati Pandita were Saiva teachers, not his guru.

88.s: Kakatiyas were feudatories of which Andhra dynasty?
88.x: The Kakatiyas first appear as Rashtrakuta vassals (Gundaya 'Rashtrakuta', Garuda emblem) and later served the Kalyani Chalukyas. The Eastern Chalukyas only issued the Magallu grant that first mentions them; they were never Kakatiya overlords.

88.s: To whom were the Kakatiyas feudatories before establishing their independent kingdom?
88.x: The early Kakatiyas were feudatories of the Rashtrakutas (Magallu: Gundaya 'Rashtrakuta'), then of the Kalyani Chalukyas. They were never vassals of the Yadavas, the Eastern Chalukyas or the Hoysalas.

88.s: To whom were the Kakatiyas feudatories before taking over the kingdom?
88.x: The Kakatiyas were originally feudatories of the Rashtrakutas (Garuda emblem) and later of the Kalyani Chalukyas (Varaha emblem). The Yadavas, Vengi Chalukyas and Hoysalas were neighbours or rivals.

88.s: Kakatiyas were subordinates of which dynasty in Andhra
88.x: The Kakatiyas were first subordinates of the Rashtrakutas, and only later of the Kalyani Chalukyas. The Eastern Chalukyas only issued the Magallu grant that first mentions them.

88.s: According to which of the following was 'Veena' the founder of the Kakatiya family?
88.x: The Bayyaram tank inscription of Mailamba traces the Kakatiyas from Venna (Venna Bhupati) as the first of the line. The Kazipet inscription names Beta I; Junagarh and Vijayawada are unrelated.

88.s: Who were the kings who had the title 'Mahamandaleswara'?
88.x: The Kakatiya rulers, as feudatories of the Kalyani Chalukyas, bore the title Mahamandaleswara (Beta II took it). It is a feudatory title, so the overlord Chalukya and Rashtrakuta kings did not use it as their style.

90.s: Whose empire was ruled by the vassals known as 'Nayakas'?
90.x: Under the Kakatiya Nayankara system the kingdom was held by military vassals called Nayakas (77 Nayankaras under Prataparudra II). The Pallavas, Yadavas and Satavahanas had no such system.

90.s: Which king introduced the Nayankara system during Kakatiya rule?
90.src: APPSC Assistant Social Welfare, Assistant BC Welfare & Assis
90.x:
Book key: Rudramba (a NextGen Level-II line says 'implemented by Rudrama'). Most books, NextGen's administration chapter and the APPSC 2025 statement question: Prataparudra (II) introduced/reorganised it into 77 Nayankaras.
The Nayankara system - military officers (Nayakas) holding Sthalas and forts for a fixed tribute - was introduced by Prataparudra II, who organised the kingdom into 77 Nayankaras. Nayakas served earlier rulers, but the system is credited to Prataparudra.

90.s: Which of the following describes the Nayankara system?
o: Military commanders were made administrators of Sthalas or Mandalams and were assigned responsibility for forts.
Temple authorities collected all taxes and maintained the royal army.
Civil scribes were appointed as village accountants without military duties.
Merchants were granted exclusive control over provincial administration.
90.x: Under the Nayankara system, military commanders served as administrators of Sthalas or Mandalams and protected specified forts.
90.tq: Identify the institutional arrangement from the roles performed by the Nayakas.
xs: Under the Nayankara system, **military commanders (Nayakas)** were made **administrators of Sthalas/Mandalams**, each protecting a **fort** — option **(1)** is correct.
It joined land control to military duty; temples, scribes and merchants had no such role in it.
xa: Nayakas received villages called **Nayakasthalam** in place of salary.
The Nayankaras controlled **one-fourth (1/4)** of the kingdom's land.
The system is compared to the Mughal **jagir**, which also linked land with military duty.

90.s: In Kakatiya military terminology, what was a 'Giridurga'?
90.x: Giridurga was a hill fort (Jaladurga water, Vanadurga forest, Sthaladurga plain); the Warangal fort had concentric walls and a moat.
xa: Other fort types: **Jaladurga** (water), **Vanadurga** (forest), **Sthaladurga** (plain).
The army had **two divisions**: **Mula Balam** (king's standing army) and the **Nayankara army**.
Each of the **72 Nayankaras** guarded a specific **fort**.

**Kavisarvabhauma** → **Srinatha**; **Kaviraja Sikhamani** → **Nannechoda**; **Andhra Kavita Pitamaha** → **Allasani Peddana**.

Potana wrote **Veerabhadra Vijayam**.
Srinatha's title was given by **Devaraya II**.

87.x: Madhura Vijayam was written in Sanskrit by Gangadevi, not by Pingali Surana. The other three pairs are correctly matched.

**Madhura Vijayam** was written in **Sanskrit** by **Gangadevi**.
Correct: **Ramabhyudayam — Ayyalaraju Ramabhadra**; **Kalahastiswara Satakam — Dhurjati**; **Rajasekhara Charitra — Madayagari Mallana**.

**Varadambika Parinayam** is by **Tirumalamba**.

87.x: Kalahastiswara Satakam is by Dhurjati.

87.x: Bhadraparinayamu was written in 1878, in the 19th century, not in the Vijayanagara period.

87.x: Statement 1 is wrong: the prabandha followed STRICT metrical rules, with a single episode, elaborate descriptions and strong shringara. Its Reddi-court beginnings (Errana, Srinatha) and peak with the Ashtadiggajas are as in the notes.

87.src: APPSC Asst. BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Mains Paper-II 2017
87.x: Donayamatya's 14th-century Sasyanandamu is the Telugu work on agricultural knowledge and rainfall forecasting; Haravilasamu is Srinatha's kavya, and Sathya Bharathi and Sasyalahari are distractors.

87.s: Telugu literature was first influenced by which empire?
87.src: APPSC Deputy Executive Information Engineers & Inspector of

Key: Vijayanagara Empire. Strictly: Telugu literature began under the Eastern Chalukyas (Nannaya); Vijayanagara gave its golden age.

87.s: Which is the first Telugu grammar, written in Sanskrit?
87.x: Andhra Shabda Chintamani, ascribed to Nannaya, is a Telugu grammar written in Sanskrit. Andhra Bhasha Bhushanam (Ketana) is the first grammar written in Telugu, Ganita Sara Sangraha is Mahaviracharya's mathematics work, and Kavyalankara Chudamani (Vinnakota Peddana) is the first alankara work.

87.s: Who wrote Appakaviyam, a Telugu grammar of the 17th century?
87.x: Appakaviyam is by Kakunuri Appakavi (17th c.); Appayacharya wrote Jinendra Kalyanabhyudayamu.

87.s:
Arrange the following periods of Telugu literature in chronological order.
A. Nannaya age
B. Tikkana age
C. Srinatha age
D. Prabandha or Rayala age
87.x: The Nannaya age belongs to the 11th century, followed by the Tikkana age in the 13th century, the Srinatha age in the 15th century and the Prabandha or Rayala age in the 16th century.
87.tq: Place the periods by their century markers, then verify the sequence from earliest to latest.
xs: Order: **Nannaya (11th c.) → Tikkana (13th c.) → Srinatha (15th c.) → Prabandha/Rayala (16th c.)** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The other orders misplace these centuries.
xa: **Shiva Kavi Yugam** (**1060-1260**) lies between the Nannaya and Tikkana ages.
**Errana age** (14th c.) sits between Tikkana and Srinatha.
After the Prabandha age: **Dakshinatya** (**17th-18th c.**) and **Modern** (**19th c.** onward).

87.s: Who is identified as the first prabandha writer in Telugu?
87.x: Errana is identified as the first prabandha writer; Nannechoda began the tradition of the eight descriptions.
xa: ⚠ Other notes call **Srinatha** the prabandha pioneer (Sringara Naishadham, Haravilasam).
CDX names **Bhaskara Ramayanam** (Hulakki Bhaskara) the first champu kavya.
The **Prabandha** age peaked with the **Ashtadiggajas** at Krishnadevaraya's court.

87.s: Which of the following literary form–example pairs is correctly matched?

87.tq: Start from the sure genre–work pair and eliminate the swapped literary forms.
xs: **Dwipada — Ranganatha Ramayanam** is correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Yakshagana** → **Sugriva Vijayam** (Kandukuri Rudrakavi); **Dvyarthi kavya** → **Raghavapandaviyam** (Pingali Surana).
**Dasakumara Charitra** is the first **story kavya**; CDX names **Bhaskara Ramayanam** the first **champu**.
xa: Ranganatha Ramayanam is by **Gona Budda Reddy**.
Raghavapandaviyam tells the **Ramayana and Mahabharata** at once.

32.s: Why did Alauddin Khilji introduce a market policy of fixed prices for food grains?
o: For better return to the farmers
To ensure that consumers can directly purchase from farmers
To ensure that the market price is equal to the fair price
To ensure that soldiers can live comfortably with low salary

32.x: Malik Kabool was a Shahna-i-Mandi, superintendent of a market.

Consider the following statements about Alauddin Khalji's market control:

4. Slave boys were used to make test purchases.

32.x: Only three (1, 3 and 4) are correct. 2 is wrong: the aim was to let a large, low-paid standing army live on fixed low prices – not lower wages for palace artisans.

32.s:
Consider the following statement connected with Alauddin Khalji :
I. He collected revenue by measuring the cultivated land.
II. He enforced revenue measures in his entire empire.
III. He abolished the powers of provincial Governors.
Select the correct answer from the coding scheme given below :
32.x: I is true – Alauddin was the first Sultan to measure cultivated land. III is accepted in the key – he took revenue under direct state control and curbed the governors' (muqtis') independent powers. II is false – measurement was limited to Delhi and the Doab.

32.s: During the regime of which Sultan was the Khalisa land developed on a large scale?
32.x: Alauddin reclaimed milk, inam and waqf grants and brought much land under khalisa (crown land) to pay his army in cash.

32.s: At what share did Alauddin Khalji fix the state's demand of produce (kharaj)?
32.x: The state share was one-half (50%); he was also the first Sultan to measure land, using the biswa.
xa: New taxes: **ghari** (house) and **charai** (grazing); **jizya** continued.
Resumed **inam** and **waqf** grants enlarged the **khalisa**.

32.s:
Consider the following statements about Alauddin Khalji's revenue reforms:
1. The privileges of khuts and muqaddams were abolished.
2. Land measurement covered the whole empire.
3. Khalisa land was expanded by reclaiming milk, waqf and inam lands.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
32.x: Intermediaries lost their privileges and khalisa grew; measurement was limited to Delhi and nearby areas.

Consider the following statements about Alauddin Khalji's revenue terms:
1. Ghari was a grazing tax on milch cattle.
2. Charai was a house tax.
3. Kismat-i-khuti, the headman's cess, was abolished.
4. Biswa was the unit of land measurement.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
32.x: Only two (3 and 4) are correct. 1 and 2 are interchanged: Ghari was the house tax and Charai the grazing tax on milch cattle.

o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A

2. He confiscated the nobles' property, religious grants and free lands.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
32.x: All three are correct: Barani lists the nobles' wealth, the weak spy system, drinking and the nobles' gatherings as causes, and an ordinance met each.

32.s: The attempt of Alauddin Khalji to control the market prices
32.x: The sources and the keys call Alauddin's market control highly successful: prices stayed fixed even in famine and the army was kept on low pay.

32.s: Alauddin Khalji’s reign is often called the ‘imperial period’ of the Delhi Sultanate mainly because it was marked by:
o: the replacement of the Sultanate by the Bahmani kingdom
the exclusive supremacy of the ulema over state policy
extensive conquests, strong centralisation and imperial ambitions

33.s: Public Works Department was primarily established by-

33.x: Firoz Tughlaq set up a Department of Public Works to look after his building programme.

33.s: Which of these Sultans set up a Department of Public Works to look after building programmes?
33.x: Firoz Tughlaq set up the Public Works Department; the other Sultans are not linked to it.

33.s: Which one of the following sultans provided employment to the unemployed?
33.x: Firoz Tughluq opened an employment office for the unemployed – not Alauddin, MBT or Sher Shah.

List-I | List-II

33.x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: Firoz banned mutilation.

33.x: Firoz Tughlaq built state canals and charged haqq-i-sharb (one-tenth of the produce); the others did not levy it.

33.s: Who among the following translated 300 volumes Sanskrit books collected by Firuz Tughluq during the campaign of Nagarkot?
33.x: The Sanskrit works taken at Nagarkot (Jawalamukhi) were translated into Persian by Azizuddin Khan (Khalid Khani) as Dalail-i-Firoz Shahi; the others are Mughal-era names.

33.x: Firoz Shah Tughlaq built the largest canal network of the Delhi Sultans (Sutlej–Hansi, Yamuna–Hisar and others).

33.s: The Sultan of Delhi who is reputed to have built the biggest network of canals in India was :
33.x: Firuz Shah Tughluq is reputed for the biggest canal network; Ghiyasuddin dug the first canals but few.

33.s: Which one of the following is NOT a town associated with Firoz Shah Tughlaq?
33.x: Firozabad, Fatehabad and Hisar Firoza were associated with Firoz Shah. Daulatabad was the renamed capital under Muhammad bin Tughlaq.

xs: **Daulatabad** is not a Firoz town — so option **(1)** is the answer.
Daulatabad was **Devagiri**, renamed by **Muhammad bin Tughlaq** (**1327**).
Firoz founded **Firozabad** (Firoz Shah Kotla), **Fatehabad**, **Hisar Firoza** and **Jaunpur**.
xa: He laid about **1,200** fruit gardens around Delhi.
He moved **Ashokan pillars** from **Topra** and **Meerut** to Delhi.

33.s: From where were the Ashokan pillars brought to Delhi during the reign of Firoz Shah Tughlaq?
33.x: Firoz Shah transported Ashokan pillars from Topra in the Ambala region and from Meerut to Delhi.
33.tq: Test the pair of source locations and reject the nearby religious and inscriptional sites.
xs: The Ashokan pillars came from **Topra** (Ambala) **and Meerut** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Jwalamukhi** at **Nagarkot** is where he seized **Sanskrit texts**, not pillars.
xa: Firoz founded **Firozabad** (Firoz Shah Kotla).
He laid about **1,200** fruit gardens around Delhi.

33.s:
Consider the following statements about Firoz Shah Tughlaq's canals:

2. His irrigation cess, haq-i-sharb, was one-fifth of the produce.
3. His canal from the Yamuna to Hisar was about 150 miles long.
4. His Rajabwah canal was restored under Akbar as the Shihab Canal.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
33.x: Only three (1, 3 and 4) are correct. 2 is wrong: haq-i-sharb was one-tenth of the produce of fields watered by royal canals.

33.s: Select the correct statements regarding the coins issued by Muhammad bin Tughlaq. a. He introduced copper and silver mixed coins described as "Adha" and "Bikh". b. He issued a new gold coin "Dinar". c. He revived "Adali" a silver coin. d. He introduced copper coin named Jital.

33.x: MBT issued a new gold coin (Dinar) and the silver Adli, so (b) and (c). Adha and Bikh were Firoz's small copper-silver coins, and the copper jital goes back to Iltutmish.

33.x: Muhammad bin Tughlaq shifted the capital from Delhi to Devagiri (Daulatabad) in 1327; Ghiyasuddin, Firoz and Nasiruddin did not.

33.x: MBT moved his capital from Delhi to Devagiri, renamed Daulatabad, in 1327 – not Kalinjar, Kanauj or Lahore.

33.x: Muhammad bin Tughlaq first introduced token currency in India (1329-30), on the model of Kublai Khan's paper money; Akbar, Alauddin and Bahlul did not.

33.s: What was the earlier name of Muhammad bin Tughlaq?
33.x: Muhammad bin Tughlaq was called Juna Khan (also Ulugh Khan) before he became Sultan; Ghazi Malik was his father Ghiyasuddin.

33.s:

33.s:
Consider the following statements about Muhammad bin Tughlaq:
1. He moved the capital from Delhi to Devagiri (Daulatabad) in 1327.

33.x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: his silver coin was the Adli; the Dinar was his gold coin.

33.s: "The king was freed from his people and they from their king". On whose death did Badauni comment thus? Medieval Indian History PMF IAS IH – 38
33.x: Badauni wrote this on the death of Muhammad bin Tughlaq (1351), not Balban, Alauddin or Firoz.

33.s: On the death of which Muslim ruler, a historian said ‘the king was freed from his people and they from their king’?
33.x: The remark is Badauni's on the death of Muhammad bin Tughlaq near Thatta in 1351.

33.s: Ibn Battuta, the Moorish traveller, visited India during the reign of :
33.x: The Moorish (Moroccan) Ibn Battuta came in 1333 under Muhammad bin Tughlaq, who made him Qazi of Delhi.

33.s: Ibn Battuta visited India during the reign of :
33.x: Ibn Battuta reached India in 1333, in Muhammad bin Tughlaq's reign (1325-51) – not Firoz's, Ghiyasuddin's or Bahlul's.

33.s: Which of the following statements about Ibn Battuta’s Rihla is correct?
o: It was written in Arabic and describes conditions in the Sultanate and the Deccan.
It was written in Persian and deals only with Central Asia.
It was written in Hindavi and describes only Vijayanagara.
It was written in Sanskrit under the patronage of Muhammad bin Tughlaq.
33.x: Rihla, also called Kitab-ul-Rehla, was written in Arabic and describes conditions in the Sultanate and the Deccan.
33.tq: Use the language-and-content combination to reject swapped literary traditions.
xs: Rihla **was written in Arabic and describes the Sultanate and the Deccan** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It is also called **Kitab-ul-Rehla**.
It was not Persian, Hindavi or Sanskrit.
xa: It records **uluq** and **dawa** couriers, the **spy system** and **sati**.
Its author, **Abu Abdullah Muhammad**, was a Moroccan born in **1304**.

33.s: In whose reign did Ibn Battuta, the first foreign traveller to Vijayanagara, visit the kingdom?
33.x: Ibn Battuta is identified in this context as the first foreign traveller to visit Vijayanagara during the reign of Harihara I.
33.tq: Distinguish the earliest associated ruler from the more famous later Vijayanagara monarchs.
xs: Ibn Battuta was the first foreign traveller to visit Vijayanagara, in **Harihara I's** reign (APPSC PYQ) — so option **(2)** is correct.
Vijayanagara was founded in **1336** by **Harihara and Bukka**.
xa: He came to India in **1333** and served MBT as **Qazi of Delhi**.
He was sent as **envoy to China** in **1342**.

33.s:
Consider the following statements about Ibn Battuta:
1. He was born at Tangiers.
2. He arrived in India in 1342.
3. Muhammad bin Tughlaq made him Qazi of Delhi and sent him as envoy to China.
4. He noted that sati was completely prohibited in the Sultanate.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
33.x: Only two (1 and 3) are correct. 2 is wrong: he arrived in 1333; 1342 is when he left Delhi for China as envoy. 4 is wrong: he noted that sati needed the Sultan's permission – it was not prohibited.

33.s:

33.x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: Barani wrote the Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi and Fatawa-i-Jahandari; the Futuhat-i-Firoz Shahi is Firoz's own account.

33.s: During Sultanate period, 'Diwan-i-Amir-Kohi' was related with which of the following?
33.x: Diwan-i-Amir-i-Kohi was MBT's department of agriculture, to bring waste land under cultivation – not the army, revenue or entertainment.

33.x: MBT created the separate agriculture department (Diwan-i-Amir-i-Kohi), which planned better crops and crop rotation in a trial block; Iltutmish, Balban and Alauddin are not linked with it.

33.s: Which ruler established 'Diwan-i-Amir-Kohi' department?
33.x: Diwan-i-Amir-i-Kohi was Muhammad bin Tughlaq's agriculture department, not Firoz's or Alauddin's.

33.s: Diwan-E-Kohi is associated with–
33.x: Diwan-i-Kohi (Diwan-i-Amir-i-Kohi) was the agriculture department of Muhammad bin Tughlaq.

33.s: How did the 'dawa' couriers of the Sultanate postal system described by Ibn Battuta travel?
33.x: Dawa were foot couriers; uluq were horse couriers.

33.s: Which rebel was Muhammad bin Tughlaq pursuing when he died at Thatta in 1351?
33.x: MBT died at Thatta on the way to Sindh, chasing the rebel Taghi after a Gujarat revolt.

33.x: Harihara and Bukka, sent by Muhammad bin Tughlaq, founded Vijayanagara under Vidyaranya's guidance.

33.x: Khizr Khan took Delhi in 1414, closing the Tughlaq period (1320-1414).

34.x: Balban followed the policy of 'blood and iron' – ruthless suppression of rebels and the nobles to restore the crown's prestige.

34.x: In 1229 the Abbasid Caliph of Baghdad sent Iltutmish a letter of investiture (mansur), making the Sultanate formally part of Dar-ul-Islam.

34.x: Alauddin Khalji did not seek the Caliph's investiture and kept religious authority out of state affairs; Iltutmish, Balban and MBT all acknowledged the Caliph.

34.x: Balban called himself 'Helper of a Caliph' in his inscription on the Garhmukteshwar mosque.

34.x: MBT's rationalist absolutism appointed non-Turks and low-born men; his coins bore 'Al Sultan Zilli Allah'.

34.x: Muhammad Ghori issued coins with Goddess Lakshmi; Mahmud of Ghazni's silver coins carried Arabic and Devanagari Sanskrit.

**Peasants** bore the revenue burden.

**Adina Mosque** and the **Pandua** mosques are the earliest Bengal examples.

37.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
37.x: The Adina Mosque is associated with Pandua in Bengal, not Gujarat. Gol Gumbaz is at Bijapur, Jami Masjid at Mandu and Chand Minar at Daulatabad.
37.tq: Check the region of each monument and locate the swapped regional association.
xs: **Adina Mosque — Gujarat** is wrong: the Adina Mosque is at **Pandua, Bengal** — option **(4)**.
Others are correct: **Chand Minar–Daulatabad**, **Gol Gumbaz–Bijapur**, **Jami Masjid–Mandu** (Malwa).
xa: **Gujarat** style: strong Hindu-Jain carving; **Jama Masjid, Ahmedabad**.
⚠ **Atala Masjid** = Jaunpur; **Adina Mosque** = Pandua (Bengal); **Gol Gumbaz** = Bijapur.

37.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Monument)
a. Adina Mosque
b. Atala Masjid
c. Jahaz Mahal
d. Chand Minar
List-II (Place)
i. Mandu
ii. Pandua
iii. Daulatabad
iv. Jaunpur
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
37.x: Adina Mosque – Pandua (Bengal); Atala Masjid – Jaunpur (Sharqi); Jahaz Mahal – Mandu (Malwa); Chand Minar – Daulatabad (Bahmani, 1435).

37.s:
Consider the following statements about provincial styles:
1. The Gujarat style shows strong Hindu-Jain carving.
2. The Gulbarga Jama Masjid has a fully covered courtyard and a large dome.
3. The Mahmud Gawan Madrasa is at Gulbarga.
4. Bengal buildings used brick, curved bamboo-type roofs and terracotta.
How many of the above statements are correct?
37.x: Three are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Mahmud Gawan Madrasa is at Bidar.

37.s: What is the name of the 16th century stepwell that the Archaeological Survey of India recently conserved in collaboration with the World Monuments Fund India?
o: More than one of the above
37.x: Rajon ki Baoli, Mehrauli (c. 1506, Daulat Khan Lodi, reign of Sikandar Lodi) was conserved by the ASI with the World Monuments Fund India (TCS Foundation funding) and reopened in May 2025. Agrasen ki Baoli and Chauki Bavdi were not this project.

37.s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Rajon ki Baoli at Mehrauli was built in the reign of Ibrahim Lodi.
Reason (R): Rajon ki Baoli was built around 1506 by Daulat Khan Lodi.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
37.x: A is false: the stepwell belongs to Sikandar Lodi's reign (Ibrahim ruled 1517-26). R is true: Daulat Khan Lodi built it about 1506.

37.s: Which of the following features is associated with Golconda Fort?
o: A fully covered courtyard and a Persian madrasa
An acoustic system and piped water supply
Curved brick roofs and a Bengal-style mosque plan
37.x: Golconda Fort is known for its remarkable acoustics and its provision of piped water.
37.tq: Identify the monument through its unusual functional features rather than its dynasty alone.
xs: **Golconda Fort** is known for its **acoustics** and **piped water** — option **(2)**.
A handclap at the gate is heard at **Bala Hisar**, nearly **1 km** away.
Covered courtyard = **Gulbarga**; curved brick roofs = **Bengal**; propylon = **Jaunpur**.
xa: **Qutb Shahi Tombs** at **Ibrahim Bagh** hold the **seven** rulers.
Golconda Jami Masjid gateway has fine **Nastaliq** calligraphy.

37.s: By which building are the minarets of the Charminar said to have been inspired?
37.x: The minarets of Sultan Quli's Juma Masjid at Golconda are said to have inspired the Charminar.

37.s:
Consider the following statements about Qutb Shahi Hyderabad and Golconda:
1. Hyderabad was founded in 1591, and the capital moved there from Golconda in 1592.
2. Hyderabad was planned on the model of Isfahan by Mir Momin Astarabadi.
3. The gateway of the Golconda Jami Masjid bears calligraphy in Naskh, and the verses round its mihrab are in Nastaliq.
4. The Qutb Shahi Tombs at Ibrahim Bagh hold seven rulers, with onion domes on square bases.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
37.x: Statement 3 is wrong: it is the other way round – the gateway is in Nastaliq and the verses round the mihrab are in Naskh.

37.s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): The Charminar marks the end of a plague.
Reason (R): Qutb Shahi architecture is an Indo-Saracenic blend of Persian and Hindu traditions.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
37.x: Both are true, but the style of Qutb Shahi buildings does not explain why the Charminar was built (to mark the end of a plague).

38.s: The first writer to use Urdu as the medium of poetic expression was:
38.x: Amir Khusrau is regarded as the first writer to use Hindavi/Rekhta, the early form of Urdu, for poetry. Ghalib, Zafar and Faiz came centuries later.

38.s: The first writer to use Urdu as the medium of poetic expression was:
38.x: Amir Khusrau is regarded as the first writer to use Hindavi/Rekhta, the early form of Urdu, for poetry. Ghalib, Zafar and Faiz came centuries later.

38.s: The savant of both languages “Hindi and Persian” was –
38.x: Amir Khusrau wrote in both Persian and Hindavi (Hindi), hence 'savant of both languages'. Akbar, Tansen and Bairam Khan are Mughal-era figures.

38.s: Father of new Persian poetry style “Sabak-i-Hindi or Hindustani style was :
38.x: Amir Khusrau created the Sabak-i-Hindi (Indian style) of Persian poetry. Barani was a historian, Afif and Isami chroniclers.

38.s: Who among the following was the first Persian poet to depict Indian environment in his poetry?
38.x: Amir Khusrau was the first Persian poet to depict the Indian environment, praising India's land, languages and people (Nuh Sipihr). Amir Hasan, Kalim and Faizi came after or were less known for this.

38.s: Amir Khusrau, the “Parrot of India,” was born at-
38.x: Amir Khusrau was born at Patiyali (1253), near Etah (now Kasganj district), Uttar Pradesh.

38.s: Who among the following is called the ‘Sadi of India’?
38.x: Amir Hasan Dehlavi (Sijzi), Khusrau's friend and compiler of Fawaid-ul-Fuad, is called the 'Sadi of India' for his ghazals. Khusrau is the 'Tuti-i-Hind'.

38.s: Which of the following is not associated with the Bhakti Movement?
38.x: Amir Khusrau was a Sufi poet (disciple of Nizamuddin Auliya), not a Bhakti saint. Vallabhacharya, Chaitanya and Guru Nanak belong to the Bhakti movement.

38.s: Who among the following is known as the ‘Father of Hindi Khari Boli?
38.x: Amir Khusrau is called the father of Khari Boli for his Hindavi riddles and verses. Jayasi wrote in Awadhi; Kabir and Rahim came later.

38.s: Amir Khusrau was a –
38.x: Amir Khusrau was poet, historian (Khazain-ul-Futuh, Tughluqnama) and musician (qawwali, tarana, sitar tradition).

38.s: Who among the following witnessed the reign of Seven Sultans of Delhi?
38.x:
Most books and keys: Amir Khusrau (court poet of seven Sultans). Strictly, Nizamuddin Auliya (1238-1325) also lived under seven or more Sultans; PMF lists five Sultans Khusrau served.
Amir Khusrau (1253-1325) lived through and served the courts of about seven Delhi Sultans, from Balban's son to Ghiyasuddin Tughluq. Nizamuddin Auliya also lived through these reigns but kept away from all courts.

38.s:
Consider the following statements about Amir Khusrau:
1. His real name was Abul Hasan Yaminuddin Khusrau.
2. He was poet laureate with a state pension under Balban.
3. He was a disciple of the Chishti saint Nizamuddin Auliya.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
38.x: Statement 2 is wrong: Khusrau was poet laureate with a state pension under Ghiyasuddin Tughluq (he was chiefly Alauddin Khalji's court poet). His real name was Abul Hasan Yaminuddin Khusrau and his guru was Nizamuddin Auliya, a Chishti Sufi.

38.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Amir Khusrau called himself Tuti-i-Hind (Parrot of India); PMF says the title was given by Alauddin Khalji.
2. Amir Khusrau is called the Father of Khari Boli, and his Hindavi riddles and verses grew into Rekhta/Urdu.
3. The title Sadi-i-Hind (Sadi of India) was given to Amir Khusrau for his ghazals.
How many of the above statements are correct?
38.x: Only statements 1 and 2 are correct. Sadi-i-Hind was Amir Hasan Dehlavi (Sijzi), honoured for his ghazals; Khusrau was Tuti-i-Hind and the Father of Khari Boli.

38.s: 'Tarikh-i-Firuz Shahi' was written by
38.x: Shams Siraj Afif wrote a Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi on Firoz Tughlaq's reign (Barani wrote the other of the same name). Yahya Sirhindi wrote Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi, Minhaj the Tabaqat-i-Nasiri and Isami the Futuh-us-Salatin.

38.s: Who is the author of "Tarikh-i-Firujshahi"?
38.x:
Two options are right: both Barani and Shams Siraj Afif wrote a Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi. Most keys give Barani; Afif (option a) is equally correct strictly.
Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi is best known as Ziauddin Barani's history (to 1357); Shams Siraj Afif wrote a second work of the same title. Isami wrote Futuh-us-Salatin and Yazdi wrote Zafarnama (Timur), so the printed key 'Isami' is wrong.

38.s:
Consider the following text and arrange them in chronological order:
1. Fatawa-i-Jahandari
2. Prithviraja-Raso
3. Kitab-ul-Hind
4. Tabaqat-i-Nasiri
Select the correct answer from the codes given below.
Codes:
38.x: Kitab-ul-Hind (c. 1030) → Prithviraja Raso (traditionally late 12th c.) → Tabaqat-i-Nasiri (c. 1260) → Fatawa-i-Jahandari (Barani, c. 1358). So 3, 2, 4, 1.

38.s:
Consider the following statements about Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi:
1. Both Ziauddin Barani and Shams Siraj Afif wrote works with this title.
2. Shams Siraj Afif's work covers the reign of Balban.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
38.x: The title has two authors, Barani and Afif; Afif's work covers Firoz Tughlaq's reign, while Barani's runs from Balban to early Firoz.

38.s:
Consider the following statements about Ziauddin Barani:
1. He held that high office should go only to the high-born.
2. He wrote his works under the patronage of Alauddin Khalji.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
38.x: Barani opposed promoting low-born men; he wrote under Firoz Tughlaq, not Alauddin.

38.s:
Match List I with List II:
List I (Work)
a. Taj-ul-Maasir
b. Futuh-us-Salatin
c. Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi
d. Zafarnama
List II (Author)
i. Yahya bin Ahmad Sirhindi
ii. Hasan Nizami
iii. Sharafuddin Ali Yazdi
iv. Isami
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
38.x: Correct code: a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii. Taj-ul-Maasir (Aibak's reign) is by Hasan Nizami; Futuh-us-Salatin (Bahmani patronage) by Isami; Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi (Sayyid period) by Yahya bin Ahmad Sirhindi; Zafarnama (Timur) by Sharafuddin Ali Yazdi.

38.s:
Consider the following statements about Muhammad Qasim Ferishta:
1. He was born at Astarabad.
2. He wrote his Tarikh-i-Ferishta (Gulshan-i-Ibrahimi) at the court of Ibrahim Qutb Shah of Golconda.
3. His account calls Telangana 'Tilang', and he is one of the writers - with Isami and Barani - who describe the fall of Warangal in 1323.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
38.x: Statement 2 is wrong: Ferishta wrote at Bijapur under Ibrahim Adil Shah II, not at Golconda. He was born at Astarabad, and with Isami and Barani he describes the fall of Warangal (1323), calling Telangana 'Tilang'.

38.s:
Consider the following statements about Ziauddin Barani:
1. He wrote both the Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi and the Fatawa-i-Jahandari.
2. His Fatawa-i-Jahandari, a work of political theory, was written in the eleventh century.
3. His Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi covers the period from Balban to the early years of Firoz (1357).
How many of the above statements are correct?
38.x: Only two are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Fatawa-i-Jahandari dates from c. 1358, the 14th century. Barani wrote both works, and his Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi runs from Balban to early Firoz (1357).

38.s:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): According to Ziauddin Barani, the state of the Delhi Sultans was not truly Islamic.
Reason (R): The Sultans ruled in practice through zawabit (state laws), and their kingship (jahandari) followed the Persian model of awe and force.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
38.x: Both are true and R explains A: Barani held that because the Sultans governed by zawabit and followed the Persian model of jahandari, their state was not truly Islamic.

38.s: Which of the following musical instruments is not of Indo-Islamic origin?
38.x:
The MPPSC 2013 official key and many books give the Shehnai. PMF credits Amir Khusrau with the Sarangi; authorities are split.
The sarangi is an indigenous Indian bowed instrument; the sitar and sarod owe their origin to Persian influence and the tabla is credited to the Indo-Islamic tradition. So the sarangi is not of Indo-Islamic origin.

38.s: ‘Tabla’ was introduced by :
38.x: The tabla is traditionally credited to Amir Khusrau. Tansen and Baiju Bawra were singers; Adil Shah is unrelated.

38.s: Musical instrument sitar is the combination of:
38.x: The sitar, traditionally credited to Amir Khusrau, combines the Indian veena and the Persian tambura (setar).

38.s: Which among the following musical instruments is the finest example of Hindu-Muslim harmony in musical instruments?
38.x: The sitar, joining the Indian veena with the Iranian tambura, is the classic symbol of Hindu-Muslim musical synthesis. The veena, dholak and sarangi are indigenous.

38.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Amir Khusrau is credited with the qaul and tarana forms and the raga Aiman (Yaman).
2. The Suhrawardi khanqahs popularised sama and institutionalised qawwali.
3. The tabla, developed from the pakhawaj, is also credited to Amir Khusrau.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
38.x: Statement 2 is wrong: it was the Chishti khanqahs that popularised sama and institutionalised qawwali. Khusrau is credited with qaul, tarana, khayal, the raga Aiman and the tabla.

38.s:
Consider the following statements about treatises on music:
1. Rag Vibodh was written by Raja Man Singh Tomar of Gwalior.
2. Ghunyat-ul-Munya (1375) is the earliest Persian treatise on Indian music.
3. Man Kautuhal is associated with Raja Man Singh Tomar of Gwalior.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
38.x: Statement 1 is wrong: Rag Vibodh is by Somnath; Raja Man Singh Tomar is linked with Man Kautuhal. Ghunyat-ul-Munya (1375) is the earliest Persian treatise on Indian music.

38.s:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): The sitar is regarded as the classic example of Hindu-Muslim harmony among musical instruments.
Reason (R): The sarangi is an indigenous Indian bowed instrument.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
38.x: Both are true, but R does not explain A. The sitar is cited because it combines the Indian veena with the Iranian tambura; the sarangi is a separate, indigenous instrument (the usual answer to 'NOT of Indo-Islamic origin').

38.s: Who among the following wrote the book 'Khazainul-Futuh'?
38.x: Amir Khusrau wrote Khazain-ul-Futuh on Alauddin Khalji's conquests. Hasan Nizami wrote Taj-ul-Maasir, Minhaj the Tabaqat-i-Nasiri and Barani the Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi.

38.s:
Which of the following texts are written by Amir Khusrau ?
1. Khazain-ul-Futuh
2. Nuh Siphir
3. Miftah-ul-Futuh
4. Qiraan-us-Sadain
38.x: All four – Khazain-ul-Futuh, Nuh Sipihr, Miftah-ul-Futuh and Qiran-us-Sadain – are Amir Khusrau's works.

38.s:
Match List I with List II:
List I (Work of Amir Khusrau)
a. Miftah-ul-Futuh
b. Qiran-us-Sadain
c. Nuh Sipihr
d. Tughluqnama
List II (Subject)
i. Meeting of Bughra Khan and his son Kaiqubad
ii. Rise of Ghiyasuddin Tughluq
iii. Jalaluddin Khalji's campaigns
iv. Mubarak Shah's reign and praise of India
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
38.x: Correct code: a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii. All four are works of Amir Khusrau: Miftah-ul-Futuh - Jalaluddin's campaigns; Qiran-us-Sadain - meeting of Bughra Khan and Kaiqubad; Nuh Sipihr - Mubarak Shah's reign; Tughluqnama - rise of Ghiyasuddin Tughluq.

38.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Khazain-ul-Futuh (Tarikh-i-Alai) describes Alauddin Khalji's early years and conquests, including the Deccan.
2. Ashiqa deals with the romance of Deval Rani and Khizr Khan, the son of Alauddin Khalji.
3. The Tughluqnama, which describes the rise of Ghiyasuddin Tughluq, was written by Ibn Battuta.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
38.x: Statement 3 is wrong: the Tughluqnama is Amir Khusrau's, not Ibn Battuta's (his travelogue is the Rihla). Khazain-ul-Futuh and Ashiqa are also Khusrau's works.

38.s: Who of the following has given a detailed description of the postal system found during the Sultanate period?
38.x: Ibn Battuta's Rihla describes the Sultanate postal system: horse post (ulaq) and foot runners (dawa) every third of a mile. Barani, Khusrau and Firoz Shah's own memoir do not give this account.

38.s: Medieval traveller and writer Ibn Batuta belonged to which country?
38.x: Ibn Battuta was a Moroccan traveller, born at Tangiers (1304); he lived in India 1333-1347 under Muhammad bin Tughlaq.

38.s:
Consider the following statements about Ibn Battuta:
1. He was born at Tangiers and reached Delhi in 1333.
2. His Rihla was written in Persian.
3. Muhammad bin Tughlaq made him Qazi of Delhi and sent him as envoy to China (1342).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
38.x: Statement 2 is wrong: the Rihla was written in Arabic. The Moroccan Ibn Battuta (born Tangiers) reached Delhi in 1333, became Qazi of Delhi and was sent to China in 1342.

38.s:
Match List I with List II:
List I (Traveller)
a. Al-Biruni
b. Marco Polo
c. Abdur Razzaq
d. Ibn Battuta
List II (Origin)
i. Morocco
ii. Venice
iii. Khwarizm (Uzbekistan)
iv. Persia - envoy of Shah Rukh
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
38.x: Correct code: a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i. Al-Biruni came from Khwarizm with Mahmud of Ghazni; Marco Polo was from Venice (Motupalli, 1292); Abdur Razzaq was Shah Rukh's Persian envoy to Deva Raya II (1443); Ibn Battuta was from Morocco.

38.s: Who among the following had translated Chintamani Bhatt’s Sanskrit text ‘Suka Saptati’ into Persian and gave it the title ‘Tutinama’?
38.x: Ziya-uddin Nakhshabi translated Chintamani Bhatt's Suka Saptati into Persian as Tutinama (14th c.). Khusrau, Abdur Razzak and al-Umari did not.

38.s: Who translated Sringaramanjari into Sanskrit?
38.x: Shay Akbar made the reverse translation of Sringaramanjari into Sanskrit.

38.s:
Match List I with List II:
List I (Work)
a. Tutinama
b. Dalail-i-Firoz Shahi
c. Kalila wa Dimna
d. Razmnama
List II (Description)
i. Persian Panchatantra
ii. Persian Mahabharata (Mughal)
iii. Based on Sanskrit texts of the Jwalamukhi (Nagarkot) temple
iv. Persian version of Chintamani Bhatt's Suka Saptati
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
38.x: Correct code: a-iv, b-iii, c-i, d-ii. Tutinama (Nakhshabi) is from the Suka Saptati; Dalail-i-Firoz Shahi from the Jwalamukhi texts under Firoz Tughlaq; Kalila wa Dimna is the Persian Panchatantra; the Razmnama is the Persian Mahabharata.

38.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Persian was the official language of the Delhi Sultanate, while Arabic was the religious language.
2. The Mahabharata and the Rajatarangini were translated into Persian under Firoz Tughlaq.
3. The Deccan form of Hindavi/Urdu is known as Dakhni.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
38.x: Statement 2 is wrong: the Persian translations of the Mahabharata and Rajatarangini are linked with Zain-ul-Abidin of Kashmir (Firoz Tughlaq is linked with the Dalail-i-Firoz Shahi).

38.s: Which one of the following Sultans of Delhi was refused an audience by Nizamuddin Auliya?
38.x:
Most books and keys: Alauddin Khalji ('two doors' reply). The saint also avoided Jalaluddin Khalji, who tried to visit through Amir Khusrau.
Nizamuddin Auliya never went to court. When Alauddin Khalji sought a meeting, he replied that his house had two doors, and if the Sultan came in by one he would leave by the other. Jalaluddin's earlier attempt (via Khusrau) also failed; Ghiyasuddin quarrelled with him ('Hanuz Dilli dur ast').

38.s:
Consider the following statements about Nizamuddin Auliya:
1. His conversations, the Fawaid-ul-Fuad, were recorded by Amir Khusrau.
2. He lived through seven or more reigns but never visited the court.
3. When Jalaluddin Khalji tried to meet him through Khusrau, he left for Ajodhan.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
38.x: Statement 1 is wrong: the Fawaid-ul-Fuad (his malfuzat) was recorded by Amir Hasan Sijzi. He never visited the court and left for Ajodhan when Jalaluddin tried to meet him.

38.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Chandayan (1379), an Awadhi premakhyan, was written by Mulla Daud.
2. Mrigavati was written by Malik Muhammad Jayasi.
3. An Urdu version of Padmavat was made by Ghulam Ali, court poet of Ibrahim Qutb Shah.
How many of the above statements are correct?
38.x: Only one is correct (statement 1). Mrigavati is by Qutban (Jayasi wrote Padmavat), and Ghulam Ali was the court poet of Abul Hasan Tana Shah, not Ibrahim Qutb Shah.

38.s: How many parvas of the Mahabharata did Tikkana render into Telugu?
38.x: Tikkana of the Kakatiya period rendered 15 parvas of the Mahabharata.

38.s: Errana of the Reddi period completed which parva of the Mahabharata?
38.x: Errana completed the Aranya Parva.

38.s: Who is the author of Sringara Naishadham?
38.x: Srinatha of the Reddi period wrote Sringara Naishadham and Kasi Khandam.

38.s:
Match List I with List II:
List I (Poet)
a. Tikkana
b. Palkuriki Somanatha
c. Gona Budda Reddy
d. Srinatha
List II (Work)
i. Kasi Khandam
ii. Ranganatha Ramayanam
iii. Nirvachanottara Ramayanam
iv. Basava Puranam
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
38.x: Correct code: a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i. Tikkana - Nirvachanottara Ramayanam (and 15 parvas of the Mahabharata); Palkuriki Somanatha - Basava Puranam; Gona Budda Reddy - Ranganatha Ramayanam; Srinatha - Kasi Khandam.

38.s:
Consider the following statements about the Qutb Shahi kingdom:
1. Telugu was used among the people and in revenue records.
2. The first Telugu farmans were issued by Ibrahim Qutb Shah and Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah.
3. Addanki Gangadhara was the first to dedicate a Telugu work to a Muslim Sultan - Tapati Samvaranopakhyanam to Ibrahim Qutb Shah.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
38.x: Statement 2 is wrong: the first Telugu farmans were issued by Abdullah Qutb Shah and Abul Hasan Tana Shah. Telugu served the people and revenue records; Addanki Gangadhara dedicated his work to Ibrahim Qutb Shah.

100.s: The Kohinoor diamond is derived from which diamond mines?
100.x: The Kohinoor was found at the Kollur mine on the Krishna (Guntur), a Golconda-kingdom mine; 'Golconda' names the kingdom and trade centre, Kollur the actual mine. Panna and Hazaribagh are elsewhere.

100.s: Who was the Qutb Shahi ruler who gave permission to the East India Company to start a factory at Machilipatnam in 1611 AD?
100.x: In 1611 the English set up their first trade centre at Machilipatnam with permission from Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah (1580–1612).

100.s: The Kohinoor diamond was found in which mines?
100.x: The Kohinoor was found at Kollur on the Krishna; Paritala is another Golconda mine, but not the Kohinoor's.

100.s: The English East India Company established a factory in the town of Machilipatnam. Who allowed the company to do that?

List II (Honour or grant from Akbar)
i. Land grant to a Parsi priest
ii. Land on which Amritsar grew
iii. Title 'Jagat Guru'
iv. Title 'Yuga Pradhan'
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
40.x: Correct code: a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i. Akbar gave the Jain Hiravijaya Suri the title Jagat Guru and Jinachandra Suri the title Yuga Pradhan; his land grant to Guru Ram Das let Amritsar grow; the Parsi Dastur Meherji Rana also received a land grant.

40.s: Who among the following was personally killed by Akbar?
40.x: Akbar personally killed Adham Khan, Maham Anaga's son, in 1562 for murdering the minister Atagh Khan.

40.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Bairam Khan:
1. Akbar gave the title of Khan-i-Khanan to Bairam Khan.
2. This title was not conferred upon Bairam Khan at the time of his appointment as wazir of the empire.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
40.x: Akbar made Bairam Khan his Wakil and gave him the title Khan-i-Khanan at that very time, so 1 is correct and 2 (not conferred at appointment) is wrong.

40.s:
Consider the following statements:
1.
Assertion (A): Emperor Akbar marched towards Afghanistan in 1581 with a huge army.
2.
Reason (R): He was on his way to reclaim his ancestral country of Ferghana in Central Asia. Options:
o: Both A and R are individually true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are individually true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
40.x: Akbar did march to Kabul in 1581, but to crush his half-brother Mirza Hakim, who backed the Bengal-Bihar rebels - not to reclaim Ferghana. A true, R false.

40.s: Akbar merged Bengal and Bihar in his empire :
40.x: Akbar defeated Daud Khan Karrani and annexed Bihar and Bengal in 1576 (conquest 1574-76).

Match
List I with

IV. 1739
